scope: 32K full-model validation of persistent sparse GPU cache residency, matched batches and 3:1 serving

revision.head: c7f1fc7960e7588afb6b8944bedac2f3e287d48b
revision.post_test_source_change: Comment clarification in _set_page_index_bufs only; executable code unchanged

fix.cause: The Python adapter removed every native Batch member after each forward, releasing GPU sparse-cache leases and clearing residency at the next attachment.
fix.behavior: Continuously scheduled requests retain native Batch membership. Only departing requests detach. Native reorder moves row bindings and flush watermarks without releasing leases; legacy host page tables receive snapshots.
fix.regressions: Request additions, removals, permutations, row compaction, stable device addresses, page-table snapshots and sparse KV data plus NVFP4 scales.

isolated_patch.description: Only residency-fix changes relative to saved local-before.patch; excludes pre-existing host sizing and flush-order changes

prefill_feed.scope: Unprofiled 32K/160 3:1 runs after the residency fix. Context prefix reuse is enabled with repeated synthetic prompts; these are not fresh unique 32K-prefill rates.
prefill_feed.definition: KV-ready means the context request's kv_cache_transfer_start timestamp, before transfer. Central window is 10% through 90% of the first-to-last KV-ready interval; all three workers use the same window.

limitations: These new full-model measurements use 1:1 prefill:decode for matched batches and 3:1 for serving, both at 32K. The 128K and 1M measurements precede this residency fix.

The initial 384 GiB/rank host-budget configuration was rejected by the smaller allocation. The successful 256 GiB/rank configuration allocates exactly the same physical sparse arena, history pools and GPU quota as the earlier matched offload run.

Exact token multisets match at controlled ready batches and across the 1696-request repeat. The 1:1 asynchronous arrivals matched 508 of 512 output sequences; every offload output sequence also appeared in resident mode. The separate 3:1 serving parity is recorded in serving.parity.
The selected 1204 and 1696 batches validate previously established capacities; this is not a new maximum-capacity search.
No GPU profiler was active in these validation measurements. Earlier profiler measurements used another node and CPU allocation and are historical references, not a controlled estimate of speedup.

cleanup.scope: Only allocations created for this task were cancelled; model controllers finished with exit code 0 before release.
